assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create a precise technical flowchart for RRSI candidate selection, wide 3:2 landscape. Match a flat ML textbook diagram style: pure white background, thin rounded outlines, very restrained pale blue/purple/orange/green fills, dark sans-serif English labels, generous spacing. Flat vector-like line art with no gradients, no photorealistic imagery, no 3D icons, no decorative title, no numerical measurements.
Every label below must be verbatim.
At the top center a blue rounded rectangle: "Screened + measured candidate".
A downward arrow goes to a blue diamond: "Historical score floor". From its LEFT a clearly labeled "Fail" arrow goes to a red outlined rounded rectangle at the LEFT margin labeled "Reject". From its BOTTOM a "Pass" arrow goes to a purple diamond centered in the image: "Gain above noise?".
This central diamond branches into TWO parallel boxes: a "Yes" arrow down-left enters orange box "Gain-dependent token allowance"; a "No" arrow down-right enters orange box "Within-band score / cost / novelty". Keep the two branches visually separate and do not connect them sequentially.
Both orange boxes have one "Pass" arrow merging into a common blue box below labeled "Domain guards". Both orange boxes also have short "Fail" arrows routed to the same left-margin Reject box. Do not cross arrows through any labels.
Domain guards has a "Fail" arrow to Reject and a downward "Pass" arrow to a green box "Admissible pool". Below that green box, an arrow goes to another green box "Choose highest score".
At the very bottom a detached gray strip reads "Empty pool: keep current harness".
At the lower right a compact pale-purple note reads "Novelty types only: tool, skill, memory, subagent". This note connects by a short dotted line ONLY to the within-band box. It is not another workflow stage.
Make Pass/Fail directions unmistakable. There must be no direct arrow from candidate to acceptance, no universal weighted ranking, and no requirement that every round must accept a candidate. No additional text, no formulas, no numbers. Ensure all text is legible and all decision edges connect to the correct box.
assets.edit_prompt:
Edit the supplied RRSI selection flowchart. Preserve ALL labels, all boxes, the white background, palette, typography, all blue Pass edges, and the two Yes/No branches exactly.
Fix ONLY the red rejection edges:
1. There are currently two red edges leaving the left side of "Domain guards". Keep exactly ONE Domain guards -> Reject edge with its "Fail" label. Remove the duplicate lower edge.
2. ADD the missing red Fail edge from "Within-band score / cost / novelty" to Reject. Route it from the bottom-right of that orange box DOWN through the whitespace to the RIGHT of the blue/green central column, then LEFT through the whitespace BELOW "Choose highest score" but ABOVE the detached gray bottom strip, then UP into the existing red rejection lane at the left. Label this new edge "Fail" along its right-side vertical segment.
It must be visibly connected to the orange within-band box; it must NOT originate from Domain guards. The new red line must avoid crossing all boxes and blue arrows. A junction with an existing red rejection lane is fine.
All three scored gates must have a rejection route: historical floor, either cost branch, and domain guards. Do not add any new text, boxes or decision rules. This is a precise edge correction.
assets.rejected_initial_reason: Missing failure edge from within-band branch; duplicate domain guard failure edge.

assets.prompt:
Create a wide 3:2 scientific concept diagram for a robotics article about contact wrench comparison. Flat vector-like textbook illustration, pure white background, thin rounded outlines, muted pastel blue/purple/orange/green, dark clean sans-serif English labels, ample whitespace. No gradients, no decorative icons, no numeric measurements. Use exactly these labels.
Three columns with the middle split into two parallel rows. On the left two separate rounded panels: upper label "Human reference contacts", showing a simple pale-blue rounded object outline with three small blue contact dots along its boundary; lower label "Robot contacts", same object outline with two orange contact dots in different boundary locations. Do not draw hands or forces. Contact dots represent geometry only.
Each left panel has a right arrow to its own matching center panel, upper blue, lower orange. Each center panel has top label "Object-frame wrench features" and below it a tiny abstract matrix icon made of six rows and several columns of dots. The upper matrix has more columns than the lower matrix. Small sublabel below both center panels: "Contact position + feasible force rays". Keep this text separate for each panel and readable.
Above the center column place one pale-purple rounded box "Shared 6D directions". Two thin purple arrows from this box go down to the RIGHT edges of each center panel, clearly feeding both feature projection paths.
From the upper center panel a right arrow goes to an upper-right green panel labeled "Reference support vector" with a single schematic row of six unequal small bars. From the lower center panel a right arrow goes to a lower-right green panel "Robot support vector" with a row of six unequal bars at the exact same x positions. These bars are qualitative, not an axis chart; do not add ticks or numbers.
The two right panels connect by simple arrows to a small common green box between them at far right labeled "Compare directions". This box has no arrow back to contacts.
At the bottom, a detached gray strip reads "Different contact counts; comparable directional capability".
Arrows must preserve reference and robot paths separately until the comparison box. Shared directions feed both paths, not only one. Contact matrices may differ in width, support vectors must have the same width. No real sensor, no exact force reconstruction, no net-wrench summation, no reward formula. All text legible; avoid overlapping paths and labels.
assets.review: Six rows in both matrices; six reference columns and four robot columns depict two illustrative rays per contact. Both support vectors show six shared directions. Actual runtime ray and basis counts are configurable; bars are qualitative.
assets.edit_prompt: Precisely edit this existing robotics contact-support diagram. Keep ALL boxes, titles, text, arrows, colors, object shapes, contact dots, support bars and layout unchanged. Correct only the small blue dot matrix in the upper middle panel labeled Object-frame wrench features. It currently has six rows and eight columns. Change it to exactly SIX ROWS and SIX COLUMNS, evenly spaced and centered in that panel. Keep the lower orange matrix at exactly SIX ROWS and FOUR COLUMNS. This makes the schematic feature-column counts proportional to the three reference contacts versus two robot contacts when each contact is represented by two illustrative ray columns. Do not add any numerical text or new labels. All other elements must remain unchanged.
